text: The central contribution of this paper is the introduction of decoupled Relative Learning Rate Schedules (RLRS) that assign distinct, cosine‑parameterized learning‑rate schedules with per‑component start/end multipliers to different Transformer modules (embeddings, attention, FFN, unembedding, and MoE experts/router), and the demonstration that this improves training efficiency, especially for MoE models. Prior work already establishes the value of non‑uniform, component‑wise learning rates: LoRA+ (Hayou et al., 2024) shows that decoupling learning rates for different parameter groups (LoRA A vs. B matrices) yields better optimization, and Everett et al. (2024) systematically study per‑layer learning‑rate prescriptions, including cosine schedules, and empirically validate that tuned per‑layer learning‑rate hyperparameters transfer across model widths. The submission’s delta lies in the specific RLRS parameterization (per‑module start/end multipliers on a shared cosine schedule), its concrete module taxonomy including MoE components, and empirical recipes for tuning on small models and applying to larger ones. However, the strongest challenged claim—hyperparameter extrapolation from small to large models—is already substantially addressed by Everett et al. (2024), and the remaining differences are mainly in scope and engineering detail rather than in conceptual core. Overall, the novelty is mixed and likely below the bar for a top venue.
verdict_summary: 1 of 3 claim(s) CHALLENGED by prior work (re-derived, fix A). Overlap degrees across claims: same x0, substantial x1, partial x4, superficial x0.
